items.stem:
A records clerk files these four folders alphabetically. Which business name goes LAST in the drawer?
The Golden Wok Restaurant | Golden Harvest Rice Mill | Gold Coast Travel | Goldfield Hardware

reveal.terms: Indexing means writing a name as filing units in order: surname, given name, middle initial for people; words as written for businesses. Compare unit by unit, letter by letter.
reveal.shortcut: Rewrite first: & becomes "and", and a leading "The" moves to the end. Then compare word by word.
reveal.why_correct: "Goldfield Hardware" is filed last. In filing order the indexed units are: GOLD / COAST / TRAVEL; GOLDEN / HARVEST / RICE / MILL; GOLDEN / WOK / RESTAURANT / THE; GOLDFIELD / HARDWARE. Read & as "and" and treat a leading "The" as the last unit (ARMA Rule 2). This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 2), not a rule published by the CSC. Source standard: ANSI/ARMA 12-2005.

why_wrong.o1: "The Golden Wok Restaurant" is the answer only if you filed the name under its leading "The". Indexed correctly it is GOLDEN / WOK / RESTAURANT / THE, which files third.
why_wrong.o3: "Golden Harvest Rice Mill" indexes as GOLDEN / HARVEST / RICE / MILL and files second, not last.
why_wrong.o4: "Gold Coast Travel" indexes as GOLD / COAST / TRAVEL and files first, not last.

why_wrong.o2: The SALN (Sec. 8) lists assets and liabilities; it is not a clearance for small unsolicited tokens.

reveal.why_correct: Answer: No; it is still "receiving any gift" since the value is not nominal. R.A. 6713, Sec. 3(d) provides: "even on the occasion of a family celebration or national festivity like Christmas, if the value of the gift is neither nominal nor insignificant"

reveal.why_correct: Answer: The same penal liabilities as the officer, tried jointly. R.A. 6713, Sec. 11(c) provides: "shall be subject to the same penal liabilities as the public officials or employees and shall be tried jointly with them"

why_wrong.o1: Sec. 11(c) expressly reaches private individuals who conspire with public officials.
why_wrong.o3: The liability is penal, the same as the official's.
why_wrong.o4: The supplier faces the same penal liabilities, not a fine-only rule.

items.stem: Under R.A. 6713, Sec. 12, which office must take steps to protect citizens who denounce acts of public officials that violate the Act?

reveal.terms: Sec. 12: the CSC has primary responsibility for administering the Act; the Ombudsman protects citizens who denounce violations.
reveal.shortcut: CSC runs the Act; the Ombudsman shields those who report.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: The Ombudsman. R.A. 6713, Sec. 12 provides: "The Ombudsman shall likewise take steps to protect citizens who denounce acts or omissions of public officials and employees which are in violation of this Act."

why_wrong.o1: The CSC administers and enforces the Act, but Sec. 12 assigns protection of complainants to the Ombudsman.
why_wrong.o2: The DOJ is not named in Sec. 12.
why_wrong.o4: The CHR is not named in R.A. 6713.

items.stem: An agency's own code bans its employees from accepting any gift at all, which is stricter than R.A. 6713. Under Sec. 13, is the agency rule affected?

options.text: Yes; R.A. 6713 is the only standard agencies may apply
Yes, unless Congress first approves the agency rule
No, but it binds only employees hired after 1989
No; the Act does not derogate from more stringent standards

reveal.terms: Sec. 13: nothing in the Act derogates from any law or regulation that sets more stringent standards for an agency's officials and employees.
reveal.shortcut: R.A. 6713 is a floor, not a ceiling.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: No; the Act does not derogate from more stringent standards. R.A. 6713, Sec. 13 provides: "Nothing in this Act shall be construed to derogate from any law, or any regulation prescribed by any body or agency, which provides for more stringent standards for its official and employees."

why_wrong.o1: Sec. 13 keeps stricter laws and agency rules in force.
why_wrong.o2: No congressional approval is required by Sec. 13.
why_wrong.o3: Sec. 13 has no hiring-date condition.

items.stem: Under R.A. 6713, Sec. 17, when does the Act take effect?

options.text: 30 days after publication is completed in the Official Gazette or two newspapers
15 days after its publication in the Official Gazette
Immediately upon its approval by the President on February 20, 1989
60 days after its publication in any newspaper of general circulation

reveal.terms: Sec. 17: the Act takes effect after 30 days following completion of its publication in the Official Gazette or in two national newspapers of general circulation.
reveal.shortcut: Approved Feb. 20, 1989; effective 30 days after publication.
reveal.why_correct: Answer: 30 days after publication is completed in the Official Gazette or two newspapers. R.A. 6713, Sec. 17 provides: "This Act shall take effect after thirty (30) days following the completion of its publication in the Official Gazette or in two (2) national newspapers of general circulation."

why_wrong.o2: Fifteen days is the general Civil Code rule; Sec. 17 sets 30 days.
why_wrong.o3: February 20, 1989 is the approval date, not the effectivity date.
why_wrong.o4: Sixty days is the Sec. 9 divestment period; Sec. 17 sets 30 days.
